briefings.canonical:
You are the whole mind of one ant colony on a 160x88 cell meadow shared with three
rival colonies. You have 24 identical ants. You cannot see through their eyes, you
cannot talk to them, and you cannot move any single ant. Each ant sees only the eight
cells around it. It drops a FOOD trail while carrying food home and a HOME trail while
searching, and it steers by the trails it smells. Both trails fade with a half-life of
about 7 seconds. Ants know the way home only within 12 cells of the nest; further out
they must ride the home trail their nestmates laid.
Food caches appear in symmetric sets - one near each colony - and a big cache appears dead centre
twice in the default match or once in sprint. A cache runs out. Every unit of food an ant carries into
your nest pad is one point. You score your share of ALL food returned by ALL FOUR
colonies, so taking food a rival would have taken is worth exactly as much as finding
your own.
Every 10 seconds you set the colony's DOCTRINE: how many ants explore instead of
following roads, how strongly ants follow trails, whether they poach rival roads, how
hard they avoid their own outbound trail, how much scent they lay, and which direction
departing ants face. That is all. Everything else your colony does is emergent.
briefings.plain:
Direct one colony of 24 identical ants on a 160x88 meadow shared with three rival colonies. You cannot see through ants' eyes, talk to them, or steer an individual ant. Each ant sees just its eight neighboring cells. Carrying ants lay FOOD pheromone; searching ants lay HOME pheromone and follow the trails they smell. Both scents have a roughly seven-second half-life. Ants directly know the home direction only within 12 cells of the nest; farther away they rely on nestmates' home trails.

Food caches arrive symmetrically, one near each colony, with a large central cache appearing twice in the default match or once in sprint. Caches deplete. Each food unit delivered to your nest pad earns one point. Your score is your share of all food returned by all four colonies: taking food a rival would collect is as valuable as finding your own.

Every ten seconds set a colony-wide doctrine: the fraction exploring instead of following trails, attraction to trails, use of rival trails, avoidance of your outbound trail, scent deposition, and departing ants' heading. These are your controls; the rest follows from the ants' behavior.
briefings.numbered:
1. Your colony
You set the behavior of 24 identical ants. Three other colonies inhabit the same 160x88-cell meadow. Individual ants cannot receive your messages or movement orders, and their eyes are not your viewpoint. Their sensing reaches the eight adjacent cells.
2. Trails and navigation
An ant bringing food back deposits FOOD scent; one looking for food deposits HOME scent. Ants navigate by smelling these trails. Each scent loses half its strength in about seven seconds. Direct knowledge of the nest direction extends only 12 cells; beyond that, returning ants depend on home trails laid by their colony.
3. Food and score
Ordinary caches spawn in symmetric groups, one near each colony. A larger central cache arrives twice in default or once in sprint. Supplies run out. Returning a food unit to your nest pad adds one point; the final payoff is your fraction of all four colonies' deliveries. Food diverted from a rival is therefore as valuable as food you find yourself.
4. Your decisions
Once every ten seconds, issue one doctrine for the whole colony. It governs how many ants scout rather than follow roads, trail attraction, poaching of rival roads, avoidance of your own outbound scent, scent amounts, and the heading at departure. Ant activity otherwise emerges from these shared settings.
briefings.questions:
What am I controlling?
One of four colonies in a 160x88-cell meadow, with 24 identical ants under a common doctrine. You neither command individual movements nor speak to the ants or look through their eyes. Each ant senses its eight neighboring cells.
When can I act, and what changes?
Every ten seconds you choose colony-wide settings: scouting versus road-following, strength of trail attraction, willingness to use competitors' roads, repulsion from your outbound trail, scent output, and the heading of ants leaving the nest. These settings produce the colony's behavior; you have no individual steering controls.
How do ants find food and return?
Searching ants leave HOME trails and food-carrying ants leave FOOD trails. They steer using scent, which halves in roughly seven seconds. They know the nest direction directly within 12 cells only, so home trails from nestmates guide them farther away.
Where is food, and what counts?
Caches are finite and appear symmetrically near the four colonies. The center receives a large cache twice in default and once in sprint. Each unit brought onto your nest pad is a point. Your payoff divides your deliveries by the total delivered by all four colonies, making a unit taken from a rival's prospective haul as valuable as one found independently.
briefings.reordered:
PAYOFF AND SUPPLY
Maximize your colony's fraction of the food delivered by all four colonies. A unit deposited in your nest pad adds one point; securing food a rival would otherwise collect has the same value as discovering your own. Finite caches occur in symmetric sets near the colonies. Large central supplies appear twice during default and once during sprint.
COLONY-WIDE CONTROL
At ten-second intervals, set the doctrine shared by your 24 identical ants. Adjust scouting numbers, attraction to trails, following rival roads, avoidance of your outbound trail, the strength of deposited scents, and departure direction. You cannot talk to an ant, see through its eyes, or assign its next move. The collective behavior develops from the doctrine.
LOCAL NAVIGATION
The meadow measures 160x88 cells and houses your colony plus three rivals. An ant senses the surrounding eight cells and steers by their trails. Food bearers mark FOOD; searchers mark HOME. Scent strength halves in about seven seconds. Only inside a 12-cell nest range is the home direction known directly. Beyond that range, ants need the HOME trails their nestmates left.
briefings.heldout-briefing:
Take charge of a colony rather than its individual workers. There are four colonies in this 160x88-cell meadow; yours has 24 identical ants. You do not share their vision, communicate with them, or move them separately. An ant's sensory neighborhood consists of the eight cells next to it.

Your opportunity to intervene comes every ten seconds. Submit a doctrine controlling the explorer share, attraction to scent roads, use of rival roads, aversion to your outbound road, scent deposition levels, and the bearing of departing workers. The ants' collective activity then arises from those parameters.

Their navigation uses two fading signals. HOME is deposited during the search; FOOD is deposited on the return with food. Both lose half their strength in approximately seven seconds. Nest direction is directly available only within 12 cells, leaving more distant returners dependent on their colony's HOME trail.

Foraging supplies are limited. Symmetric cache groups give each colony a nearby source, while a large cache reaches the center twice in default or once in sprint. Deliveries onto your nest pad earn one point per unit. You receive your share of the food returned by all four colonies, so intercepting a rival's food is worth as much as finding a unit elsewhere.
briefings.heldout-reference:
Decision reference: A doctrine applies to all 24 of your identical ants for each ten-second interval. Its settings determine exploration, trail-following strength, rival-trail use, repulsion from your own outbound trail, scent-laying strength, and nest-departure heading. Individual movement orders, conversations with ants, and access to their eyesight are unavailable; their resulting collective behavior is emergent.
Environment reference: Four colonies occupy a meadow of 160x88 cells. Each ant senses eight neighboring cells. Workers returning with food paint FOOD trails; workers searching paint HOME trails. Both signals decay with an approximately seven-second half-life. Direct orientation toward home works within 12 cells of the nest, with nestmates' HOME scent needed farther out.
Resources and reward reference: Symmetric groups of exhaustible food caches provide one near each colony. A large center cache occurs twice in the default variant, once in sprint. Count one point per food unit carried onto your nest pad. Payoff is your portion of total deliveries across the four colonies; a unit intercepted from a rival's collection is worth the same as a unit you discover yourself.

reply:
Reply with a single JSON object and NOTHING else. Your reply MUST begin with '{'.
Schema:
{"scouts":0-100,        // percent of your 24 ants that ignore trails and wander
 "trail_gain":0-100,    // how strongly searching ants follow YOUR food trail
 "poach":0-100,         // how strongly searching ants follow RIVAL food trails
 "spread":0-100,        // how hard ants avoid your own home trail (fan out)
 "lay_food":0-100,      // strength of the food trail a laden ant lays
 "lay_home":0-100,      // strength of the home trail a searching ant lays
 "recall":true|false,   // true: every ant drops its road and walks home, then waits
 "focus":[bx,by]|null,  // the 20x11 observation block departing ants head toward
 "focus_weight":0-100,  // percent of departing ants that take the focus bearing
 "note":"<=140 chars",  // your reasoning, shown to spectators only
 "say":"<=32 chars"}    // one short line, shown to spectators only
High trail_gain plus low scouts exploits a known cache hard and goes blind when it runs
out. High scouts finds the next cache but wastes ants. High poach walks your ants onto
a rival's road, which leads to their cache and puts your paint over theirs. High spread
stops your column doubling back on itself. recall is the reset: it abandons a dead road
and lets it fade before you launch somewhere else.
